# Holiday Events Around LCF You Don't Want to Miss

There is something truly magical about spending the holidays in the foothills. While Southern California may not bring snow-dusted pine trees naturally, La Cañada Flintridge and its surrounding communities know how to celebrate the season with grand light displays, beloved community traditions, world-class theater, and historic parades. Whether you are looking for an energetic morning run, an evening stroll under illuminated oak trees, or a festive night out at the ballet, here are the can't-miss holiday events across our local area this season.

---

## La Cañada Flintridge

Our hometown holiday celebrations start bright and early on Thanksgiving morning with the annual [CCLCF Thanksgiving Run & Food Drive](https://runsignup.com/Race/Events/CA/LaCaadaFlintridge/CCLCFThanksgivingRun) (the local Turkey Trot), which rallies runners and walkers of all ages at Olberz Park to kick off the festive season while supporting local food banks and community center programs. As the calendar turns to winter, the town’s crown jewel comes alive with the [Enchanted Forest of Light at Descanso Gardens](https://www.descanso-gardens.org). This internationally acclaimed nighttime walk transforms the gardens' iconic botanical collections into an immersive wonderland of glowing stained-glass village installations, responsive kinetic light fields, and illuminated ancient oak groves that enchant visitors of every generation.

## Glendale

Just down the Verdugo Mountains, Glendale offers a festive blend of classic downtown glitz and stage entertainment. A stroll through [The Americana at Brand](https://americanaatbrand.com/) delivers quintessential holiday spectacle: one of Southern California's tallest Christmas trees, dancing fountain shows choreographed to holiday favorites, visits to Santa’s House, and magical nightly artificial snowfalls that draw crowds to the green. For performing arts lovers, the historic 1925 Art Deco [Alex Theatre](https://www.thealex.com/) hosts grand holiday productions throughout December, including classic stagings of Tchaikovsky’s *The Nutcracker* presented by visiting world ballet companies and local youth troupes alike.

## Old Pasadena & Downtown Pasadena

Pasadena turns on the charm with its garland-draped brick alleys and historic architecture. An evening in [Old Pasadena](https://www.visitpasadena.com/events/annual-events/rose-parade-guide/) offers boutique shopping, courtyard dining under twinkle lights, and seasonal access to architectural gems like the historic Castle Green holiday tours along South Raymond Avenue. Theater and music lovers can catch Charles Dickens’ holiday classic brought to vibrant life at [A Noise Within](https://anoisewithin.org/) during their annual production of *A Christmas Carol*, or experience the transcendent [Holiday Candlelight Concert by the Pasadena Symphony](https://pasadenasymphony-pops.org/) beneath the Gothic arches of All Saints Church.

## Griffith Park & The L.A. Zoo

Just a short drive over the 134 freeway into the edge of Griffith Park, [L.A. Zoo Lights: Animals Aglow](https://lazoo.org/plan-your-visit/special-experiences/zoolights/) provides one of the region’s premier seasonal spectacles. This self-guided nighttime adventure guides visitors through luminous glowing wildlife lanterns, kinetic color tunnels, synchronized light fields, and festive photo stops, complete with hot chocolate and churro carts along the way. It makes for an ideal evening outing for families wanting a glowing, festive walk that is mere minutes from the foothills.

## Tournament of Roses

No foothills holiday season is complete without the grand finale that puts our backyard on the international stage: the [Tournament of Roses Parade](https://tournamentofroses.com/about/about-rose-parade/). Rolling down Colorado Boulevard each New Year’s, this century-old tradition showcases floral-covered floats, high-stepping equestrian units, and elite marching bands from around the globe. Local residents also have the unique privilege of visiting [Decorating Places](https://www.visitpasadena.com/events/annual-events/rose-parade-guide/) in the days leading up to the parade to witness volunteers painstakingly placing millions of petals, bark, and seeds onto the floats before they make their famous turn down Orange Grove.
